A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPGym research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 Figures 3–4 report original five-seed experiments with PPO and DreamerV3, including pretrained-encoder and decoder-gradient variants.

after.justification: v3 reports original PPO, SAC and DreamerV3 experiments, including unseen-image evaluation, additional puzzle configurations and sensitivity analyses in Section 5 and Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: Section 3 changes the stated solved-puzzle reward from +10 to +1 and revises Manhattan-distance normalization. This changes the benchmark's learning signal locally; image-pool construction, tile movements and the two initialization procedures remain substantially unchanged. Expanded descriptions of retained agents do not establish architectural changes.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates 3×3 puzzles using ImageNet-1k validation images. v3 adds DiffusionDB images, 4×4 PPO puzzles and direct evaluation of trained policies on unseen images (Section 5, Figure 5, Tables 3–4). The latter goes beyond v1's encoder-transfer experiments, which involved training on the new image pool.

E2.justification: v3 retains the three PPO and two DreamerV3 variants and adds discrete SAC plus RAD, CURL, SPR, DBC, SAC-AE, SAC-VAE and Simple Baseline variants to the reported comparisons (Tables 1–2). RAD and CURL were discussed but explicitly not evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: Reported PPO environment instances change from 1,024 to 64 and rollout steps from 4 to 16; DreamerV3 replay capacity changes from 5 million to 500,000 (v1 Table 1; v3 Tables 7 and 9). v3 also revises sampled pool sizes and adds 100-episode unseen-image evaluation, episode-length metrics and a control without early stopping. These are reported protocol changes, without establishing which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond retained pretraining and decoder-gradient comparisons, v3 adds SAC representation-component comparisons, entropy-temperature/autotuning sweeps and augmentation ablations (Appendix C, Figures 7–8). Section 5 additionally examines unseen-image generalization and tests whether continued PPO training after successful convergence improves solution length.

E5.justification: Sample-efficiency uncertainty changes from v1 Figure 3's bootstrap confidence intervals with 1,000 resamples to v3's mean ±1.96 standard errors. v1 already used normal-based intervals for learning curves, and both versions retain five independent seeds for the main comparisons; increased replication is not reported.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial numerical results: at pool size 5, SAC+RAD requires 0.42M steps versus SAC's 0.91M and DreamerV3's 1.23M (Table 2); unseen-image success is near zero, and 4×4 PPO success is 51.4±39.3% (Tables 3–5). Existing curves are revised and some entries, including v1's 500-image DreamerV3 result, disappear. Changed settings prevent same-setting cross-version performance claims. Some PPO success values disagree between v3 Tables 3 and 5.

T1.justification: v3 introduces an explicit POMDP specification and revises the reward mathematics in Section 3. In particular, its normalization expression omits v1's explicit exclusion of the blank tile. These are limited formal changes; neither version develops theorem or proof results.

C1.justification: The benchmark's central scalability and representation-learning claims remain, but v3 adds prominent claims that several specialized representation methods underperform standard SAC and that trained agents generally fail to transfer to unseen images. Its introduction and conclusion substantially broaden v1's principal empirical message about DreamerV3 outperforming PPO and degradation with visual diversity.

C2.justification: v3 adds method-specific hypotheses for CURL, DBC, SPR, SB and VAE failures, interpretations of augmentation benefits, and an early-stopping versus solution-quality tradeoff (Section 5 and Appendix D.1). It newly qualifies comparisons by architectural differences and limited tuning. The earlier limitation about missing representation-focused agents is replaced, while the five-seed limitation remains.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands implementation documentation with preprocessing, architectures, augmentation procedures, auxiliary optimization and SAC hyperparameters, plus a separate experiment-code link. Appendix D.2 adds SAC runtimes and revises PPO's longest reported runtime from 30 to 90 minutes. Some details conflict: Table 10 lists crop-based augmentations, whereas Section 4 and Appendices B–C specify grayscale and channel shuffling.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially to puzzle benchmarks, including Estermann et al., classical heuristic search and deep-RL puzzle solvers. Additional literature supports SAC and its representation-learning variants. Several earlier references, including DrQ, CBM, CycAug and two puzzle-solving sources, disappear. This substantially revises positioning relative to closely related puzzle research.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, benchmark description, results and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Results are reorganized around five research questions, benchmark mechanics receive named subsections, and appendices expand into A–F with hyperparameters moved to E. The NeurIPS checklist is removed, while acknowledgements and a dedicated impact statement are added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one to two columns. v1's combined sample-efficiency chart becomes separate algorithm panels in v3 Appendix Figure 9, and scaling curves gain a SAC panel. v3 adds visual-diversity and augmentation illustrations, result tables and analysis plots. The existing modality illustration is retained and renumbered from Figure 2 to Figure 3.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly lacked representation-focused comparators and left direct unseen-image testing to future work. v3 addresses both central gaps and adds analyses of augmentation, tuning and solution quality, supported by much fuller implementation documentation. This substantially strengthens the benchmark's empirical assessment. Conflicting PPO success summaries in Tables 3 and 5 and augmentation instructions in Table 10 reduce confidence in specific details, but the broader evidence and diagnostic analyses provide a substantial net improvement.
